professors.name: Fei-Fei Li
professors.title: Sequoia Capital Professor of Computer Science; Founding Co-Director, Stanford HAI
professors.biography: Official Stanford CS profile states that Dr. Fei-Fei Li is the inaugural Sequoia Professor in the Computer Science Department and a Founding Co-Director of Stanford's Human-Centered AI Institute. She served as Director of Stanford's AI Lab from 2013 to 2018. The profile identifies her as inventor of ImageNet and the ImageNet Challenge.
professors.research_summary: Official profile describes current research in deep learning, robotic learning, spatial intelligence and ambient intelligence for healthcare delivery, with prior work in cognitive and computational neuroscience.

professors.name: Percy Liang
professors.title: Professor of Computer Science; Director, Center for Research on Foundation Models; Senior Fellow, Stanford HAI
professors.biography: Official Stanford CS profile states that Percy Liang is a Professor of Computer Science and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI, and director of the Center for Research on Foundation Models (CRFM). He received a B.S. from MIT (2004) and Ph.D. from UC Berkeley (2011).
professors.research_summary: Official profile states current focus on making foundation models, in particular language models, more accessible through open-source and understandable through rigorous benchmarking. Past topics include robustness, interpretability, human interaction, learning theory, grounding, semantics and reasoning.

professors.name: Chelsea Finn
professors.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science and of Electrical Engineering
professors.biography: Official Stanford CS profile states that Chelsea Finn is an Assistant Professor in Computer Science and Electrical Engineering and the William George and Ida Mary Hoover Faculty Fellow. She received a bachelor's degree from MIT and a Ph.D. in Computer Science from UC Berkeley.
professors.research_summary: Official profile describes research on enabling robots and other agents to develop broadly intelligent behavior through learning and interaction, including end-to-end learning of visual perception and robotic manipulation, deep reinforcement learning, and meta-learning.
